title: Design of a loading system for cyclic test on sutured organs
author: Pascoletti, Pressanto, et al.

steps.title: Define system requirements
steps.instruction: List the main requirements for the loading system: compatibility with a standard testing machine (Instron Electropulse E3000), axial loading of the suture, on‑site testing to include anchorage compliance, versatility for various organ shapes, high stability and stiffness for repeatable results, and feasibility using readily available or easily manufactured components.

steps.title: Select loading concept
steps.instruction: Choose the dual‑pulley concept that overcomes the pinching configuration problems. The concept uses a massless wire, static loads, negligible friction, and provides wire tension equal to half the machine force (F/2). Ensure the upper pulley diameter D satisfies D = r1 + r2 + i, where r1 and r2 are the radii of the lower pulleys and i is the distance between their centres.

steps.title: Design component layout
steps.instruction: Create a detailed design of each component: (1) Support Base with perforated plates (weight >20 kg, allows bolting the organ), (2) Support Plate soldered on the base to raise lower pulleys, (3) Support Bar with a slot for horizontal positioning of lower pulleys, (4) Lower Pulley pair whose height is adjustable to load the thread along its axis, (5) Upper Pulley fixed to the actuator of the testing machine.

steps.title: Analyse support‑base stability
steps.instruction: Perform static‑force and overturning‑moment calculations. Use FA as the external force applied by the machine (maximum 100 N) and Fw as the weight force of the base. Vertical equilibrium: FA – Fw = 0 → FA = Fw. Overturning moments about x‑ and z‑axes: –Fw(zP–zCM) + FA(zP–zA) = 0 and –Fw(xP–xCM) + FA(xP–xA) = 0. Insert the most unfavourable coordinates (xCM=0 mm, yCM=47.8 mm, zCM=0 mm; xA=42.9 mm, yA=194.8 mm, zA=–2.05 mm; xP=–125 mm, yP=0 mm, zP=80 mm) to obtain: –Fw·80 + 100·82.05 = 102.56 N and –Fw·(–125) + 100·(–167.9) = 134.32 N. The second condition is most restrictive, giving a minimum base mass Mb = Fw / g = 13.7 kg.

steps.title: Select base dimensions
steps.instruction: Based on the stability analysis, adopt the following geometry for the support base: length Lb = 250 mm, diameter db = 160 mm, height Hb = 80 mm, hole depth hb = 62 mm, and lower‑plate offset lb = 50 mm. Drill perforations in two plates to allow bolting the organ.

steps.title: Fabricate and assemble system
steps.instruction: Manufacture the support base (≥20 kg) to the chosen dimensions, weld the two perforated plates onto it, solder the support plate on top, attach the slotted support bar, mount the adjustable lower pulleys at the desired height, and fix the upper pulley to the actuator of the Instron Electropulse E3000. Verify that the assembled system weighs at least 13.7 kg and that the pulley geometry satisfies D = r1 + r2 + i.

steps.title: Validate loading performance
steps.instruction: Connect the system to the testing machine, apply a known force F (up to 100 N) and confirm that the tension measured in the suture wire equals F/2 and that T1 and T2 remain horizontal regardless of anchorage point migration.
